text:
mira: Heads-up: ran a quick canary for sirocco-v2 q4f on the multilingual eval set. Seeing a weird cluster of failures centered on U+200A (hair space) + Arabic ligature contexts.

mira: Short numbers: ja BLEU 23.1 (-2.9), zh BLEU 29.4 (-0.3), ar BLEU 17.6 (-4.6). The AR regressions correlate with ligature sequences like \u0644\u0627 (lam+alef) when preceded or followed by hair space or U+200F.

kai: Hair space? That's new. Any chance preprocessing normalized it into regular space?

mira: No, tokenizer preproc explicitly preserves hair space for CJK kerning tests. But the embedding indices in int8 build map a few ligatureish tokens to adjacent ids.

devon: That sounds like an off-by-one in the compressed vocab index table on quant path. We had a change to pack special token groups into a compact table for q4f.

ash: @devon can you confirm whether the compact table keeps the same order as the canonical vocab? We added a remap layer during onboarding but tried to keep it transparent.

devon: Quick check: remap preserves lexical order except we fold whitespace variants into a single entry for size savings. Hair space was folded with NBSP in the remap. If the remap layer didn't get applied upstream of the index translation for the int8 runtime, tokens could be shifted.

mira: Repro steps I ran:
1) baseline: sirocco-v2 fp32 + tokenizer v2 -> baseline outputs
2) canary: sirocco-v2 q4f + tokenizer v2 -> observed bad mirroring/ligature loss
3) canary2: sirocco-v2 q4f + tokenizer v1 -> smaller delta

mira: Minimal failing example (AR):
Input: "\u0627\u0644\u0628\u064a\u062a\u200a\u0644\u0627\u0646"  (contains U+200A between tokens)
Output int8: "\u0627\u0644\u0628\u064a\u062a \u0627\u0644\u0627\u0646"  (ligature split or replaced with ascii space)

eva: Can you dump token id sequences for input vs output on both fp32 and int8? I want to see whether the model emits the wrong token id or if detokenization broke.

mira: Uploading traces to S3 now. Will include token id lists and raw logits for the span.

kai: @eval-bot run a quick compare focusing on hair-space and rtl ligature samples across the canary sweep. Mark token-level substitutions.

eval-bot: Compare job queued: compare-hairspace-1765464321. Results pending.

devon: Alternative quick triage: re-run q4f artifact with the remap disabled (force remap_passthrough=true) to see if fold/unfold remapping is the culprit. If that fixes, we can hotfix runtime to disable folding for canary.

mira: Will try remap_passthrough and also run with fp32-emulate kernel like last time.

ash: If it's a remap bug, we need a short-term mitigation: 1) pin tokenizer v1 for q4f canary until we fix remap, 2) add an eval rule to detect whitespace-folding substitutions that break ligatures.

eva: I'll add a synthetic test to the harness that injects hair/thin spaces inside Arabic ligature runs and fails the canary if BLEU drops > 2.5 or token-substitution rate > 1%. ETA end of day.

mira: Action list:
- mira: run remap_passthrough and fp32-emulate tests + upload traces (ETA 90m)
- devon: audit remap layer and compact table packing for hair-space/NBSP folding (ETA EOD)
- eva: add synthetic hair-space ligature tests to eval harness and canary gating (ETA EOD)

eval-bot: compare-hairspace-1765464321 started. Link: https://ci.redwood/sirocco/compare/1765464321

mira: FYI I also noticed a small uptick in JP space-insertion around ruby annotations when hair-space present; adding that to repro set.

kai: Good catch. Might be shared folding rule across CJK and RTL pipelines.

mira: If we hit a blocker, we should consider pausing the q4f rollout for staging until remap audit completes.

ash: Agreed. Keep ops on standby in case we need an emergency rollback.

eval-bot: compare-hairspace-1765464321 finished: summary: AR BLEU -4.5, JP BLEU -3.1, flagged 97/120 hair-space ligature anomalies. Detailed token diffs uploaded. Link: https://ci.redwood/sirocco/compare/1765464321/results

mira: Thanks all. I'll sync after the remap audit and post recommended canary config.
